title: Multiple Representations of Relationships

authority.learning_target: Students will connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
authority.intro: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
authority.review: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.
authority.mastery: Solve inequalities, represent solution sets graphically, and interpret solutions in context.

language_focus: specific nouns/quantities when context is used
question_structure_ideas: Give a table and ask students to choose the matching graph/equation, then justify with two ordered pairs.
Give a graph and a nearly matching table with one wrong row; locate and correct the mismatch.
Start from a context with a starting value and constant change; build table -> equation -> graph.
Give two representations with different scales and ask whether they still represent the same relationship.
Translate between two representations, then require a short evidence statement showing the connection.
Turn a named misconception into an error-analysis or distractor family rather than inventing arbitrary wrong answers.
Use reverse reasoning at least occasionally: provide a result/feature and ask for a possible input, rule, representation, or condition.
When context adds meaning, use real quantities and units; otherwise use a clean mathematical prompt with no fake story.
math_note_ideas: Equivalent representations preserve the same input-output pairs even when they look different.
Use two checkpoints to test equivalence: a shared ordered pair and a shared rate/pattern.
Scale changes appearance, not the underlying relationship.
table_data_ideas: input-output table paired with equation and graph
same relationship shown with altered graph scale
figure_representation_ideas: coordinate graph paired with a small value table
context graph with labeled axes and meaningful units
misconception_targets: Matching representations by visual appearance while ignoring scale or values.
Changing a table or graph without preserving the same ordered pairs or relationship.
modeling_context_seeds: Build a graph from a context about distance, cost, or time.
Formulate an equation from a table of values.
Use a graph to predict a missing table value.
Check whether a context and equation communicate the same relationship.

Give a table with a repeated input and ask whether it can represent a function.

Translate between two representations, then require a short evidence statement showing the connection.
Turn a named misconception into an error-analysis or distractor family rather than inventing arbitrary wrong answers.

Ignoring interval conditions in a piecewise rule.

title: Modeling Investigation

authority.learning_target: Students will create and analyze mathematical models using real-world data.
authority.intro: Create and analyze mathematical models using real-world data.
authority.review: Create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
authority.mastery: Use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.

language_focus: specific nouns/quantities when context is used
question_structure_ideas: Use a real dataset to choose a model, estimate parameters, validate with graph/table, and interpret.
Require students to state assumptions and limitations.
Compare two plausible models and defend a choice.
Translate between two representations, then require a short evidence statement showing the connection.
Turn a named misconception into an error-analysis or distractor family rather than inventing arbitrary wrong answers.

Revise a model when the data or domain makes the first model weak.
Interpret parameters and outputs in the original context.

Written interpretation of model parameters and limits

title: Function Synthesis and Capstone Analysis

authority.learning_target: Students will synthesize understanding of function families and representations to solve complex problems.
authority.intro: Synthesize understanding of function families and representations to solve complex problems.
authority.review: Write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
authority.mastery: Solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula and interpret solutions.

language_focus: specific nouns/quantities when context is used
question_structure_ideas: Synthesize multiple representations and families in one comparison task.
Use a capstone scenario requiring model choice, interpretation, and communication.
Give competing claims based on the same data and ask students to evaluate them.
Require transfer to a less-familiar representation without adding needless computation.
Translate between two representations, then require a short evidence statement showing the connection.
Turn a named misconception into an error-analysis or distractor family rather than inventing arbitrary wrong answers.
Use reverse reasoning at least occasionally: provide a result/feature and ask for a possible input, rule, representation, or condition.
When context adds meaning, use real quantities and units; otherwise use a clean mathematical prompt with no fake story.
math_note_ideas: Synthesis means choosing and connecting tools, not merely performing every procedure in the course.
Evidence should be communicated with equations, tables, graphs, and contextual interpretation as appropriate.
misconception_targets: Choosing a representation by habit rather than by the information needed.
Combining results from different representations without checking that they describe the same relationship.

Synthesize evidence from several function families to solve a problem.
Revise a model or solution when a representation reveals a conflict.
Communicate why a chosen model or strategy fits the problem conditions.
framework_representations: Tables, equations, and contexts used together
Written reasoning about model choice and solution meaning
